I don't know if there's any truth to the notion, but it's been said
that diligently writing a clan newsletter can help one become a
playtester. At the very least, it's a way to contribute to the V:TES
community. As such, it might help you demonstrate to the
development team that you have a solid understanding of the
game and have the time an energy to contribute as a playtester.

I think either Peter Bakija or Lasombra is keeping track of what
clan newsletters are looking for writers.

- Ben Peal

Messages.Author: pd...@lightlink.com
Messages.Body:
The Lasombra wrote:
> No, neither of us is really keeping track. However, at a quick
> glance, the following clans have never had newsletters written for
> them:

It really was just too much work, as the list was constantly changing,
and really, the best way to keep track is to see who wrote one in the
last few months.

For those feeling dubious about writing clan newsletters, in the sense
of "Eh, I really got nothing new to say...", here is why Clan
Newsletters are good, regardless of whether or not they are discovering
amazing new ideas or not. Clan Newsletters are very easy to access,
easy to find, concentrated strategy information that does not require
duking it out on usenet or whatever. That TheLasombra archives all
these things is both awsome (thanks again, Jeff!) and incredibly
useful, as new players, or not new but non usenet inclined players can
find acres of easy to follow, easy to digest, concentrated strategy
ideas for their favorite clans. White Wolf has a bunch archived (or did
last I checked), but seems to have stopped picking them up (Oscar, is
there a way I could, I dunno, be enabled to put new ones up there?).
But in eaither case, archived Newsletters are a valuable resource for
the game community as a whole. Even if they aren't wildly innovative.

-Peter

Messages.Author: Fabio 'Sooner' Macedo
Messages.Body:
Ben Peal escreveu:

> I don't know if there's any truth to the notion, but it's been said
> that diligently writing a clan newsletter can help one become a
> playtester. At the very least, it's a way to contribute to the V:TES
> community.

Well, I know at least one former clan newsletter editor who got to
start a playtesting group and one playtester that did the other way
round - i.e., became a newsletter editor *after* a couple of
playtesting opportunities.

With that in mind, I'd say writing a newsletter certainly helps to
attract attention. But participating in this group and demonstrating
knowledge and interest seems to be key; it doesn't matter that much in
what form (writing a newsletter or just plain work, such as helping new
players, commenting rules, suggesting new cards etc.)

Fabio "Sooner" Macedo

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


What you and others have said in this thread is fairly accurate.

Playtesters are chosen from the online community (this NG, the WW
forum, &c.) based on their ability to demonstrate critical thought on
the rules and cards and to demonstrate the excess of free time to build
and analyze decks necessary to playtesting, to a degree that attracts
my attention. Writing a series of good newsletters is certainly a big
plus in the qualifications column, but it is not a requirement.
